question: Why was a carbonate electrolyte used with the sodium metal anode of the sodium-sulfur battery?
rendered: The excerpts do not mention a carbonate electrolyte being used with the sodium metal anode of the sodium-sulfur battery. In fact, it is mentioned that the battery uses a glyme-based electrolyte, specifically NaPF6 salts dissolved in tetraglyme, to overcome the unstable SEI formation on Na metal anodes observed in carbonate-based electrolytes.
